Orchards and roadside sellers around Ishwardi in May–June
ishwardi-litchi.desc: Around Ishwardi, villages are thick with litchi trees, and for a few weeks in late spring and early summer the fruit turns the trees red. Bombai is the most common variety, with Mozaffarpuri and China-3 also grown. Traders buy fruit straight from the orchards, and roadside stalls sell bunches tied with string. A fresh litchi eaten under the trees tastes nothing like one that has travelled for days.
blocks: Good to know
The season is short, roughly mid-May to mid-June, so plan ahead.

glance: White sweets about 260 BDT per kg
Kori Pal's sweet shop, Arambaria Bazar, Ishwardi upazila, Pabna
ishwardi-kori-pal-doi.desc: Four brothers have run this small sweet shop at Arambaria Bazar in Ishwardi together for about four decades, after their father Gopinath Pal died soon after independence. It has no signboard; everyone simply calls it Kori Pal's shop, after the eldest brother. Its doi is what people come for. It is made only as far as the day's milk allows, so it usually has to be ordered ahead. The shop also makes a full range of sweets and supplies most weddings and events in the area.
blocks: Good to know
Order doi a day ahead; walk-in stock runs out fast.

glance: 205 km to Pabna by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
gajnar-beel.desc: Gajnar Beel is the largest wetland in Sujanagar upazila, formed by sixteen smaller beels joined together and touching all its unions. Water comes from the Padma, the Jamuna and the Chalan Beel system, and the Badai sluice gate at Sagarkandi links it to the Padma. In the rainy season it turns into a wide sheet of water crossed by boats, and in the dry months the land is farmed. Fishing and farming here keep much of Sujanagar going.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus from Pabna to Sujanagar, then an auto-rickshaw towards the beel or the Badai sluice gate at Sagarkandi.
Good to know
Hire a local boat in the monsoon and wear a life jacket. Go in the late afternoon for the light over the water.

glance: 205 km to Pabna by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
chatmohar-shahi-mosque.desc: Chatmohar Shahi Mosque dates from the late 16th century, the era of the Bengal Baro-Bhuiyans, and is attributed to Masum Khan Kabuli. Its thick brick walls and three domes have been restored and it is still used for prayers. Chatmohar itself sits on the southern edge of Chalan Beel, so the trip can be combined with the wetland in the rainy season. Few outside visitors come here.
blocks: How to get there
Chatmohar is on the railway line north of Pabna; from the station take a rickshaw to the mosque.
Good to know
Dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

glance: 205 km to Pabna by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
jor-bangla-temple-pabna.desc: This temple on the north-east side of Pabna town follows the jor bangla style, in which two curved-roof hut forms are joined side by side. It dates from the 1850s and is dedicated to Gopinath, a form of Krishna. Traces of terracotta decoration remain on the facade. It is small but a good example of how Bengali temple builders turned village house shapes into sacred architecture.
blocks: How to get there
About 2 km north-east of central Pabna; take a rickshaw and ask for the Jor Bangla mandir.
Good to know
Combine with Suchitra Sen's house in the town centre.

glance: 205 km to Pabna by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
taras-bhaban-pabna.desc: Taras Bhaban, also called Taras Rajbari, was built in Pabna town by Raibahadur Banamali Roy, zamindar of Taras, during British rule. Its style follows the European Renaissance, with a big entrance flanked by pairs of tall columns and decorated walls. The main block is about 100 feet long and 60 feet wide. Over the years it housed government offices and even Pabna Medical College for a while, and in 1998 the Department of Archaeology declared it a protected monument.
blocks: How to get there
It is in the centre of Pabna town; walk or take a rickshaw.
Good to know
You can often only see it from outside. Combine it with the Jor Bangla Temple and Suchitra Sen's house in town.

Trusted sweet and dairy shops in Pabna town
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
pabna-ghee.desc: The low-lying pastures of southern Pabna and neighbouring Sirajganj support many small dairy farms, and Pabna's ghee has a strong reputation across Bangladesh. It is made by slowly heating butter until it turns golden and nutty, and is drizzled over hot rice, khichuri or polao. Many families still make it at home, and local shops sell it in tins and jars. Good ghee has a grainy texture and a rich, slightly toasty smell.
blocks: Good to know
Buy from established shops; adulterated ghee is a common problem.

pabna-handloom-hosiery.desc: Handloom weaving has long been an important cottage industry in Pabna, producing sarees, lungis and gamchhas on wooden looms in village homes. In the 20th century the town also became known for small hosiery workshops making vests, socks and knitwear. Walking through weaving neighbourhoods you can hear the clack of looms and see yarn being dyed and dried in the sun. Many weavers are happy to show their work to respectful visitors.
blocks: Good to know
Ask a local guide or rickshaw driver to take you to a weaving para near town. Buy directly from weavers if you can.

shitlai-rajbari.desc: Shitlai Rajbari, also called Shitlai Zamindar Bari, stands in Shitlai village in Nimaichara union of Chatmohar upazila. Its foundation is dated to around 1734, under zamindar Jogendranath Maitra, whose estate covered much of the Chatmohar area. The complex has three single-storey buildings and one two-storey building, next to a big tank known as Hemanta Sagar. It is a quiet place, and the old walls by the water are a good stop on a Chatmohar heritage day with the Shahi Mosque and Handial temple.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or train to Chatmohar, then an auto-rickshaw to Shitlai village in Nimaichara union.
Good to know
Parts of the house may be in use or in poor repair, so ask before going inside.

glance: 205 km to Pabna by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
suchitra-sen-house.desc: Suchitra Sen, one of the most celebrated actresses of Bengali cinema, was born in 1931 and spent her early years in this house on Hemsagar Lane. After a long legal dispute the district administration took it over, and it was opened to visitors in 2017. Photographs and memorabilia recall her life and films. Fans of classic Bengali cinema will find it a touching stop.
blocks: How to get there
In central Pabna on Hemsagar Lane; rickshaw drivers know it as Suchitra Sen's house.
Good to know
Check opening hours locally, as they can change.

handial-jagannath-temple.desc: The Jagannath temple at Handial lies about 18 km south of Chatmohar town. It is a small one-door brick temple whose walls carry terracotta decoration, and it is protected as an archaeological monument. Scholars date it anywhere from the 15th to the mid-16th century, and an inscription records a repair by one Bhabaniprasad in 1590. Two newer temples stand beside it inside a walled compound, along with a small chariot, and worship continues here.
blocks: How to get there
From Chatmohar take a CNG or auto-rickshaw south to Handial.
Good to know
Remove shoes and ask before photographing inside. The Rath Yatra festival is the liveliest time.

hardinge-bridge.desc: The Hardinge Bridge spans the Padma between Paksey in Pabna and Bheramara in Kushtia, and was one of the great engineering works of its time. Its row of steel truss spans was damaged in the 1971 war and later repaired. Beside it runs the modern Lalon Shah road bridge, and the riverbank between the two is a popular spot to watch trains rumble across. In the dry season, sandbanks appear below and you can walk out on them.
blocks: How to get there
Go to Paksey in Ishwardi upazila by bus or train; the riverbank is a short walk from the station area.
Good to know
Do not walk on the railway bridge itself. Late afternoon gives the best light and passing trains.
